final_assistant_text:
Your own estimates are in the model, but none of them sits on the path that decides this comparison, so these figures are still provisional. A share of runs in which an option fitted your goal better than the others is not the chance of reaching your target.

The key failure stories are extra delivery costs without enough additional billable work.

1. Imagine ‘Hire two developers’ went badly because ‘Revenue foregone from delivery-cost burden’ reduced ‘monthly revenue’. The added payroll consumed resources without enough additional revenue to offset the burden. Watch for: Payroll rose while invoiced revenue stayed flat. Mitigate: Review committed billable work against the added payroll before making offers.

2. Imagine ‘Hire two developers’ went badly because unfilled delivery capacity meant ‘Delivery capacity’ did not translate into ‘Billable delivery days’. Olumi’s estimated capacity and billable-day figures overstated what the team actually sold and delivered. Watch for: Available developer days increased while booked client days did not. Mitigate: Validate the capacity and billable-day assumptions against signed work and recent utilisation.

Outside the model: Could a security incident have stopped client work altogether?
